# CV Axle Replacement Procedure

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove wheel, lift vehicle, detach caliper and rotor, lower control arm, swap old for new CV axle, then reassemble components. [t867]

[Partial] Shove the new CV axle into place, using a second person to fan-angle components as needed. [t867]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the wheel and set it aside.
2. Lift the connected wheel off the ground using a jack, then secure the vehicle with jack stands for safety.
3. Loosen the 32mm nut on the CV axle by first removing its cotter pin and saving it.
4. [Partial] Use a breaker bar with the 32mm socket to fully remove the loosened nut from the hub.
5. Remove the brake caliper by taking off two bolts located on the back of the spindle.
6. Support the freed caliper with zip ties or similar means so it does not hang by the brake line.
7. Pull the brake rotor off and set it aside to clear access for the lower control arm.
8. Raise the lower control arm level using a bottle jack to facilitate CV axle removal.
9. Detach the tie rod from the spindle by removing its cotter pin first, then loosening the nut.
10. Use a ball joint separator tool if necessary to free the tight tie rod shaft from the spindle.
11. Unplug the ABS sensor wire connector and detach it from the frame by prying it out.
12. Remove the upper control arm's cotter pin and save it for later use.
13. [Partial] Loseen the nut on the upper ball joint shaft and separate it from the spindle, using a separator if needed.
14. Lower the spindle so its top points outward and away from the vehicle body.
15. [Partial] Flex the CV at both joints to remove the threaded end of the old axle from the hub and spindle.
16. Pull the free-ended CV out of the differential by overcoming the spring clip with several firm pulls.
17. Clean the area on the differential where the new CV will sit using a clean rag.
18. Insert the splined (non-threaded) end of the new CV into the cleaned differential opening.
19. Flex the new CV joints to thread its shaft through the hub and spindle assembly.
20. Screw the 32mm bolt onto the threaded end of the newly inserted CV shaft.
21. Reinsert the upper control arm's ball joint shaft into the spindle and tighten the nut.
22. Secure the upper control arm by reinstalling or replacing its cotter pin.
23. [Partial] Plug the ABS sensor wire connector back into its receptacle on the new axle assembly.
24. Reattach the detached ABS sensor wire to the frame.
25. Insert the tie rod's ball joint shaft into the spindle and tighten the nut securely.
26. Secure the tie rod by reinstalling or replacing its cotter pin.
27. [Partial] Lower the bottle jack supporting the lower control arm, then remount the brake rotor over it.
28. [Partial] Reattach the brake caliper to the back of the spindle without putting tension on the line.
29. [Partial] Tighten the 32mm nut while a helper applies pressure with their foot or hand against the brakes.
30. [Partial] Finish the job by installing the cotter pin into the tightened 32mm nut.

_Procedure reported by [t867]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-replace-a-cv-axle.6432/>_

2. [Partial] Shove the new CV axle into place, using a second person to fan-angle components as needed.

## Tools

- Lug nut wrench [t867]
- Jack and jack stands [t867]
- Bottle jack [t867]
- 32mm socket [t867]
- 17, 19, and 21mm wrenches/sockets [t867]
- Breaker bar [t867]
- PB Blaster or penetrant oil [t867]
- Ball joint separator (pickle fork) [t867]

## Tips & gotchas

- The right and left CV axles are identical and can be interchanged. [t867]
- Use a helper to apply brakes while loosening the large nut on the axle shaft. [t867]
- Leave the brake caliper mounted on the rotor in cases where clearance allows it for simplicity. [t867]
- [Partial] Use butt connectors or wire nuts with tape instead of soldering if cutting wiring is required to avoid resistance changes. [t867]
